# GPU Procurement Guide — November 2026

*Data as of 2026-11-18. All prices in USD per GPU-hour unless noted.*

---

## 1. Executive Summary

The GPU cloud market is in a **tightening phase**. Across 15 of 17 tracked SKUs, on-demand averages have risen 15–70% over the past four quarters. The notable exceptions are **GB200** (down 21% from its June peak) and **RTX-4090** (down 9.5% month-over-month), both signaling supply catch-up in their respective segments.

NVIDIA stock sits at **$153.78** (−18.6% YTD, near its 52-week low of $148.80), while AMD has surged **+123.7% YTD to $500.00**. This divergence is reflected in pricing: AMD MI300X/MI325X now deliver the best FLOPS-per-dollar in the market, and new US export restrictions (capping Chinese customer share at 49% of Nvidia data-center business) are reshaping supply chains.

**Bottom line:** If you need sustained capacity for >3 months, lock in reserved or 1-year commitments *now* before the Q1 2027 demand spike. If your workload is bursty or experimental, the Vast.ai / RunPod spot layer is 40–65% below on-demand averages.

---

## 2. Reserved vs. Spot / On-Demand: Decision Framework

### When to Commit to Reserved / 1-Year Instances

| Signal | Threshold | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Utilization | >60% sustained for 8+ weeks | Reserve. You're paying for idle capacity at on-demand rates. |
| Price trajectory | On-demand avg rising >10% QoQ (true for B300, B200, H200, H100-SXM, A100-80GB) | Lock a 1-yr reserved rate *before* the next quarterly repricing. |
| Prediction-market signal | Implied price 6+ months out is **higher** than today (H200: $2.99 now → $7.62 implied Dec '26) | Buy reserved now; the market is pricing in a supply crunch. |
| Regulatory risk | US tightening remote-access controls; Nvidia capping Chinese customer share at 49% | Diversify across ≥2 providers; a single-provider reserved contract is a concentration risk. |
| Workload type | Training runs, fine-tuning pipelines, multi-week RL loops | Reserved. Spot interruption mid-epoch is costlier than the discount you'd save. |

**Rule of thumb:** If your expected monthly spend at on-demand exceeds **$15,000/GPU** (≈ 5,000 hrs × $3 avg), the 20–35% reserved discount on hyperscalers (AWS, GCP, Azure, Oracle) or 15–25% on neoclouds (CoreWeave, Crusoe, Lambda) pays for itself within the first 60 days.

### When to Stay on Spot / On-Demand

| Signal | Threshold | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Utilization | <30% or highly variable (batch inference, CI/CD, research experiments) | Spot. You'll be interrupted more than you're running. |
| Price trajectory | On-demand avg falling (GB200: $19.51 → $15.42 over 4 qtrs) | Wait. Prices are still compressing. |
| Workload type | Inference serving with auto-scaling, data preprocessing, eval sweeps | Spot + checkpointing. Vast.ai and RunPod spot pools are 40–65% below on-demand. |
| GPU generation | You're on a generation that's being superseded (A100, H100-PCIe) | Don't reserve. Migrate to the next gen on spot and re-evaluate in 2–3 months. |
| Vendor lock-in risk | Single-provider dependency >70% of spend | Keep at least 30% on a second provider's spot pool. |

### The "Hybrid" Play (Recommended for Most Teams)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  BASE LAYER (60-70% of capacity)                        │
│  → 1-yr Reserved on CoreWeave / Crusoe / Lambda         │
│  → Locks in ~20-30% below current on-demand avg         │
│  → Covers your steady-state training / serving load      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  BURST LAYER (30-40% of capacity)                       │
│  → Spot / On-Demand on Vast.ai, RunPod, Together AI     │
│  → 40-65% below on-demand avg                           │
│  → Auto-scales for evals, A/B tests, traffic spikes     │
│  → Checkpoint every 5 min to survive preemption         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
